xp_rules: Defence XP only from quest rewards at this stage (current Defence is 1; all Defence XP at this stage comes from quests)
Never train Defence directly or choose Defence for an XP lamp or other choosable XP reward
Never use a combat style that gives Defence XP (e.g. defensive, or controlled/shared melee styles; longrange ranged or defensive-casting magic)
Total Defence XP from all quest rewards used must keep Defence at or below the cap (50); the XP engine tracks this on every route

intro: Hardcore Worlds: almost every death ends the run, including many that are safe for a Hardcore Ironman. Each step lists what can kill you and how to prepare.
Danger badge: the big number is the score without prep; 'with prep' is what the prep card buys. The Fractured Archive = one hundred, the top of the scale.
Route hours exclude all quest time; no verified source gives quest durations.
Balanced is not faster than Safest. Choose it for its quests (lyre to Rellekka, Tirannwn, quest Defence), not for speed.
Standing rules: Defence only from quests; Ranged on Rapid or Accurate; dismiss every random event; no AFK, player-owned house, Nightmare Zone, Rogues' Den maze, poison chalice or Wilderness.
Profit is at the Hardcore Worlds GE mid price, assuming every mark is sold, before any GE tax; the Graceful outfit ({{fact:F-4004}} marks) is not deducted.
outro: Werewolf Agility Course is blocked: the deathslide's maximum fall damage is unpublished. It lifts when Agility and Strength pass the never-fail point, or a source publishes the maximum.
Sins of the Father and the Hallowed Sepulchre are blocked: the quest's fights were never researched. It lifts after a research request and a Risk Officer re-rating at your stats.
The Graveyard and its new course are announced but not released, so they are not in this guide. Never choose Defence on its lamps.
Prayer up before the fight, not during it. When the card says stop, stop.

steps.title: The Writing's on the Wall (Quest Month, released 3 Nov 2026)
steps.location: Starts with Betty at Land's End; visits Port Piscarilius prison
steps.rationale: Fixed 2,500 Agility XP with no required kills (the ambush is a cutscene, F-3086/F-5014) and no Defence XP, so it is safe for the Defence-50 cap. Done first, at 57, because fixed quest XP replaces the slowest training of the whole route (Falador, 57-60). Its 2,500 Thieving XP also lifts Thieving 24 to at least 26 (tools/xp.py), part of the way to Death on the Isle's Thieving 34 (DP04 option C). New content (17 days old at verification): re-check the walkthrough before release; the prison cell is teleport-blocked (F-5014).
steps.why_not_faster: Training straight through would avoid the quest's travel and walking time, but this quest has no documented damage source and its XP lands where the route's XP rate is lowest; its only danger signal is that it is under 30 days old.

prose.summary: New quest (under a month old) with a teleport-blocked prison cell. Gives {{step.xp_gained}} fixed Agility XP, no required kills and no Defence XP.
instructions: Read the current wiki walkthrough end to end. If it lists any fight, aggressive monster or damage source not on this card, stop and ask for a re-rating.
Bank: mid-heal food from the card and one teleport usable outside the prison cell.
Gear: normal non-Defence setup; the quest needs no combat.
Travel: start with Betty at Land's End, at full HP.
Do: follow the quest. The ambush is a scripted knock-out cutscene, not a fight.
Do: in the Port Piscarilius prison cell, do not teleport. Remove the plank, climb through the north-wall gap and walk clear of the guards first.
Stop: when the quest completes. The Thieving reward moves you toward Death on the Isle's requirement.
warnings: Mandatory: re-read the walkthrough on the day you start. This is new content and its two dungeons were not reviewed. Anything new on the page means stop and get a re-rating.
Mandatory: start at full HP with the card's food and a teleport. Never enter the prison area below {{risk.min_hitpoints}} HP.
The prison cell blocks teleports. A guard who catches you sends you back in; the plank and north-wall gap are the only way out.
Stop condition: if you lose HP in a dungeon and cannot see why, leave at once (exact line in 'Stop immediately if').
Stop condition: dismiss every random event. A death inside one is official on Hardcore Worlds.
Any death here is official and run-ending; no Hardcore Worlds safe exception covers this quest.
tips: Headline {{risk.inherent_ds}}, with prep {{risk.residual_ds}} ({{risk.tier}}). Held up by the new-content floor, not by known damage.

hazards.description: Brand-new quest (released 3 Nov 2026, under 30 days old): the walkthrough is still being edited and its two dungeons were not reviewed for aggressive NPCs.
Port Piscarilius prison cell is teleport-blocked; the exit is a plank and a gap in the north wall, and being caught by a guard returns you to the cell.
The ambush is a scripted knock-out cutscene, not a fight; no kills are listed.

lethality.rationale: No documented damage source, but the quest visits two dungeons whose walkthrough was not reviewed for aggressive monsters and the page is still changing. Rated 2 rather than 0/1 because absence of documentation is not proof of safety.

pvp.rationale: Kourend and Land's End; no Wilderness.

escape.rationale: The prison cell blocks teleports; you leave only through the wall gap, and guards send you back.

attention.rationale: Quest dialogue and sneaking past guards; periodic attention.

disconnect.rationale: No combat documented; a disconnect is at worst a lost step.

unpredictability.rationale: Brand-new mechanics (under 30 days old) per the anchor.

knowledge.rationale: Content under 30 days old; T2-only requirements; walkthrough not reviewed end to end.

mitigations.action: Re-read the current wiki walkthrough on the day you start; if it now shows any fight, aggressive monster or damage source not listed here, stop and ask for a re-rating before continuing.
Start at full HP with 6+ food and a teleport for use outside the cell; never enter the prison area below 40 HP.

steps.title: The Depths of Despair
steps.location: Great Kourend (Crabclaw Caves section is instanced)
steps.rationale: Fixed 1,500 Agility XP, no Defence XP, prerequisites already complete. The only required kill is a Sand Snake (level 36, max hit 3, safespottable along the west wall, F-5016), trivial against 48 Hitpoints. Placed at 57 with the other low-danger quest because fixed XP is worth most where training is slowest. Bring a little food: the Crabclaw stepping stones and rocks can be failed and their damage is undocumented (F-5384).
steps.why_not_faster: Skipping it saves the quest's travel time, but the 1,500 XP comes from a fight with a max hit of 3, so it adds almost no danger to the safest route.

prose.summary: Short Kourend quest for {{step.xp_gained}} fixed Agility XP. The only kill is a weak Sand Snake you can safespot.
instructions: Bank: bow and arrows for the safespot, the few mid-heal food on the card, and a teleport.
Gear: Ranged on Rapid or Accurate, never Longrange; Longrange gives Defence XP.
Travel: Great Kourend. The Crabclaw Caves section is an instance.
Do: be at full HP before every stepping stone and rock; eat back to full after any fall.
Do: fight the Sand Snake only from the west-wall safespot. Go north or south along the west wall, then hug it back to the centre entrance.
Stop: when the quest completes. To leave the caves early, walk out and teleport once outside the instance.
warnings: Mandatory: fight the snake only from the west-wall safespot with Ranged. Stop condition: if the safespot fails and the snake reaches you, leave the cave.
Mandatory: full HP with food before the stepping stones and rocks; their fall damage is unpublished.
Stop condition: stop and eat if HP falls to the card's eat line.
Do not rely on a teleport inside the cave; whether it works there is not stated. Walk out first.
tips: Prerequisites are already done; fixed XP is worth the most where training is slowest.

hazards.description: Sand Snake (level 36, max hit 3, aggressive) in the instanced Crabclaw Caves; safespottable along the west wall.
Crabclaw Caves stepping stones and rocks can be failed; fall damage is not published.
Whether you can teleport from the cave is not stated.

lethality.rationale: Snake max hit 3 (6% of 48 HP). Obstacle fall damage is unpublished; rated conservatively at 2, not 1.

escape.rationale: Instanced cave section; teleport behaviour not stated.

attention.rationale: Safespot positioning and obstacle crossings need constant attention.

disconnect.rationale: Aggressive snake: a 60-second in-combat disconnect at Defence 1 could cost most of 48 HP (max 3 every attack).

unpredictability.rationale: RNG damage within known bounds for the snake.

knowledge.rationale: Obstacle fall damage and cave teleport behaviour are undocumented.

hw_death_classification.note: Not on the T1 safe list.

mitigations.action: Fight the Sand Snake only from the west-wall safespot with Ranged (go north or south along the west wall, then hug it back to the centre entrance).
Be at full HP with food before crossing the stepping stones and rocks; eat back to full after any fall.

stop_conditions: Stop and eat if HP falls below 30
Leave the cave if the safespot does not hold (snake reaching you)

risk.bailout: Walk back out of the Crabclaw Caves section the way you came and teleport once outside the instance; do not rely on a teleport inside the cave.

necessity.why: Fixed 1,500 Agility XP with prerequisites already done; worth most at 57 where training is slowest.
safer_alternatives: Skip it and train the XP on Falador (S08)

risk.verdict_reason: Low danger with a documented safespot; the snake's damage is small and the only unknown is obstacle fall damage, covered by the full-HP rule.

steps.title: Icthlarin's Little Helper

requirements.name: A cat or kitten from Gertrude's Cat

steps.rationale: Fixed 4,000 Agility XP and no Defence XP (F-2061 also lists Thieving 4,500 and Woodcutting 4,000, not carried as numbers here because no fact holds them as a value). Fights: the Possessed Priest (max hit 6, Protect from Magic stops his damage, F-5029) and one apparition (max hit 6-9; protection prayers protect fully). Placed in the 57 quest block because it is the prerequisite for A Tail of Two Cats (S04), whose two lamps are the larger reward. Danger to note: once a flashback starts you cannot teleport until it ends (F-2064/F-5030); logging out is the exit. Dying also loses the cat.

prose.summary: {{step.xp_gained}} fixed Agility XP and the key to A Tail of Two Cats' lamps. Danger: teleport-blocked flashback fights; the right protection prayer makes them safe.
instructions: Bank: the card's food, full waterskins, an antipoison, prayer restores, your cat or kitten, and Ranged gear.
Gear: Ranged on Rapid or Accurate, never Longrange; Longrange gives Defence XP.
Travel: magic carpet across the desert with full waterskins. Never walk the River Elid banks or north of Sophanem.
Do: examine the canopic jar before the pit jump; it sets which guardian you face.
Do: start each fight with full prayer and hold it to the end: Protect from Magic for the Possessed Priest and Apmeken, Protect from Melee for Het or Scabaras.
Do: in Klenter's Pyramid, cure scarab poison at once with antipoison.
Stop: when the quest completes, then go on to A Tail of Two Cats.
warnings: Headline {{risk.inherent_ds}}, with prep {{risk.residual_ds}} ({{risk.tier}}). No teleport works during a flashback. A disconnect with no prayer up is what kills; the correct protection prayer fully protects.
Mandatory: enter each flashback at full HP and full prayer with food. If prayer or HP falls to the card's lines, walk back toward the entrance, or log out once unhit long enough.
Stop conditions: do not start a flashback with prayer under the card's line; leave if HP falls to the card's line; never start the pit jump before examining the jar.
Mandatory: desert travel by carpet with waterskins only. The River Elid and the area north of Sophanem mean heat and aggressive crocodiles.
Stop condition: dismiss every random event. A death inside one is official on Hardcore Worlds.
A death here is official on Hardcore Worlds and also loses your cat.
tips: Worth it for the Agility XP and the gate to A Tail of Two Cats and its two lamps.
Safer choice: decision point `DP02` option A skips this block.

hazards.description: Possessed Priest (91, max 6, magic/crush); Protect from Magic stops his damage.

Second-flashback apparition (Het max 9 slash, Apmeken max 6 magic, Scabaras max 8 slash), set by the canopic jar; protection prayers give full protection. Teleports are blocked once a flashback starts.
Klenter's Pyramid: wall crushers (damage not quantified), pit traps, mummies (84), scarab swarms (2 damage plus poison).
Desert travel: heat 1-10 every 24-132 s outside towns; aggressive level 63 crocodiles (max 6) along the River Elid and north of Sophanem.

lethality.rationale: Apparition up to 9 (19% of 48), heat up to 10, scarab poison stacking; crusher damage unknown.

escape.rationale: No teleport during a flashback; exit is walking back or logging out (only out of combat).

attention.rationale: Correct protection prayer per guardian, traps and poison.

disconnect.rationale: A disconnect without prayer inside the flashback leaves you in combat for up to 60 s against a guardian hitting up to 9 at Defence 1: likely fatal.

unpredictability.rationale: Guardian identity is weighted, not certain; random scarab swarms.

exposure.rationale: A long quest with desert travel: a few hours.

knowledge.rationale: Crusher damage unquantified; Possessed Priest max hit single-page.

hw_death_classification.note: Not on the T1 safe list. A death also loses the cat.

mitigations.action: Examine the canopic jar before the pit jump. Keep Protect from Magic on for the Possessed Priest and for Apmeken, Protect from Melee for Het or Scabaras, for the whole fight; start each fight with full prayer.
Enter the flashback at full HP and prayer with food; if prayer drops below 15 or HP below 30, walk back toward the entrance (or log out once 16 ticks have passed since the last hit).
Desert travel by magic carpet with waterskins; never walk the River Elid banks or the area north of Sophanem.
Carry an antipoison for scarab swarms in the pyramid.

required_items: prayer restore or full prayer before each flashback
stop_conditions: Stop if prayer is below 15 before a flashback
Leave the flashback if HP falls below 30
Do not start the pit jump without having examined the jar
Dismiss any random event in the pyramid or a flashback; never accept one there

risk.bailout: Inside a flashback you cannot teleport: walk back to the entrance with your protection prayer on, or log out once out of combat to be placed outside the pyramid. In the desert, carpet back to Shantay Pass.

necessity.why: Fixed 4,000 Agility XP and the prerequisite for A Tail of Two Cats (S04, 5,000 Agility XP in lamps).
safer_alternatives: DP02 option A: skip the quest block and train on rooftops

risk.verdict_reason: High unmitigated because a disconnect inside a teleport-blocked flashback without prayer is likely fatal; with the correct protection prayer held through each fight (which the guardian facts say gives full protection) it drops to Low. Full prep card applies.

steps.title: A Tail of Two Cats (both lamps into Agility)

No required kills (F-2071). Done straight after Icthlarin's Little Helper while the cat and desert travel are fresh. Items: 5 death runes, a chocolate cake (buy it to avoid the Cooking 50 route) and a cat (F-2069).

instructions: Bank: death runes, a chocolate cake (buy it), your cat or kitten, a few food and full waterskins (counts on the card).
Gear: light travel gear; no fight is required.
Travel: magic carpet across the desert. Never walk the river banks or north of Sophanem.
Do: follow the quest; the dragon scenes are cutscenes.
Do: rub both lamps and choose Agility, never Defence.
Stop: when both lamps are spent and the quest is complete.
warnings: Mandatory: both lamps go into Agility (or another non-Defence skill). Never click Defence.
Mandatory: carpet-only desert travel with full waterskins. Stop condition: leave the desert if your waterskins run out.
Stop condition: if the quest asks for a fight not described here, stop and ask for a re-rating.

hazards.description: No required kills (inferred from the missing kills field); dragonkin and KBD scenes are cutscenes.
Travel to Sophanem crosses the desert (heat) and crocodile areas.

disconnect.rationale: No combat; heat stops when you leave the game.

unpredictability.rationale: Heat damage within known bounds.

Put both lamps into Agility (or another non-Defence skill at 30+); never Defence.

Leave the desert if waterskins run out

steps.title: Underground Pass
steps.location: West Ardougne to the Underground Pass (whole quest instanced)

requirements.name: A bow and 1-5 non-poisoned metal-tipped arrows (no crossbows)

steps.rationale: Fixed 3,000 Agility XP and no Defence XP (F-2045 also lists 3,000 Attack, not carried as a number). Its real value is the gate to Regicide (S06, 13,750 Agility XP). All required fights are safespottable from Ranged (owner Ranged 56): demons max hit 9, paladins 8, Kalrag 9 and blocked by Protect from Melee. The hazards are traps (up to 24 on a failed bridge jump, F-5026/F-5379) and blessed spiders that pile on after Kalrag dies (F-5024); plan full HP before bridges and Kalrag. Placed in the 57 block so Regicide's large fixed XP lands before the slow 57-60 training.

prose.summary: {{step.xp_gained}} fixed Agility XP and the only door to Regicide. Dangers: failed bridge jumps, spiders after Kalrag, Iban's temple spikes. Required fights can be safespotted.
instructions: Bank: a large stack of food (minimum on the card; no bank beyond the Pass), prayer restores, an instant teleport, a bow with non-poisoned metal-tipped arrows, and Ranged ammunition.
Gear: Ranged on Rapid or Accurate, never Longrange; Longrange gives Defence XP.
Travel: West Ardougne to the Pass entrance. The quest is an instance; any instant teleport exits.
Do: be at {{risk.min_hitpoints}} HP or more before every Iban's Lair bridge jump, the rope swing and the Kalrag fight. Eat at the card's eat line.
Do: safespot the demons from the narrow pathways and the paladins by attacking and running west, with Ranged. Keep Protect from Melee on for Kalrag.
Do: use the plank on wall traps and never stand in front of an armed trap. After Kalrag dies you are briefly stunned; leave the spider corridor at once.
Do: enter Iban's temple at full HP and run in without stopping. After a spike stun, step back, eat to full, then retry.
Stop: when the quest completes, or teleport out when a stop condition below is met.
warnings: Headline {{risk.inherent_ds}}, with prep {{risk.residual_ds}} ({{risk.tier}}). Worth it as the gate to Regicide, the largest Agility reward available today, and later the elf chain toward Prifddinas.
Mandatory: never jump a bridge or take the rope swing below {{risk.min_hitpoints}} HP. A failed jump hits hard and lands you among aggressive Soulless.
Mandatory: Iban HP gate. Protect from Melee does nothing against the temple spikes. Enter only at full HP and never retry hurt; after any spike stun, eat to full first.
Stop condition: if the spikes stun you back to the entrance twice in a row, or food is below the card's temple reserve, teleport out and restock.
Stop conditions: teleport out if HP is at the card's line with no food, or more than three monsters attack at once. If stunned among spiders, eat first, then teleport.
Never stand in front of an armed wall trap; it can hit repeatedly and fast enough to kill.
Stop condition: dismiss every random event. A death inside one is official on Hardcore Worlds.
tips: Read the current card before you go; the earlier owner acceptance of this card is on record.

hazards.description: Iban's Lair bridge jumps fail about 16% of the time at Agility 57-58 for up to 24 damage and drop you among aggressive Soulless; the north rope swing fails for up to 14.
Wall traps 5-14 on a failed disarm; standing in front of an armed trap 'will repeatedly hit very fast and could be fatal'; grid pits 15; swinging logs 6-13.
Three demons (91, max 9), three paladins (62, max 8), Kalrag (89, max 9, blocked by Protect from Melee); blessed spiders (max 4) pile on, and killing Kalrag stuns you about two seconds.
Whole quest is instanced; any instant teleport can be used to leave.

Iban's temple entrance: red spikes deal about 5-8 each, rapidly, are NOT blocked by protection prayers (Protect from Melee does nothing here), stun you and return you to the entrance. The number of hits per attempt is not published. A player who arrives after the Kalrag corridor at low HP and retries without eating can take several stun-locked hits.

lethality.rationale: A failed bridge jump can deal 24 (50% of 48 HP) and is followed by Soulless; spiders pile on after Kalrag; repeated wall-trap hits 'could be fatal'; Iban's spikes hit 5-8 rapidly through prayer with a stun, number of hits unpublished.

escape.rationale: Instance, but any instant teleport leaves; long walk otherwise.

attention.rationale: Constant attention: safespots, traps, HP before every jump and before the temple, one protection prayer for Kalrag.

disconnect.rationale: A disconnect after a bridge fall or in the spider corridor keeps you in combat up to 60 s with several attackers.

unpredictability.rationale: Many jumps make at least one fall likely; spider pile-ups behave like multi-combat; spike hit count unpublished.

exposure.rationale: A long dungeon quest: a few hours.

knowledge.rationale: Bridge damage figure is internally inconsistent (24 vs 20%+5); several max hits single-source; spike count unpublished.

hw_death_classification.note: Not on the T1 safe list.

mitigations.action: Be at 40+ HP before every Iban's Lair bridge jump, the rope swing and the Kalrag fight; eat whenever below 35 (24 is the conservative bridge bound).
Safespot the demons from the narrow pathways and the paladins by attacking then running west, with Ranged; keep Protect from Melee on for Kalrag.
Use the plank on wall traps and never stand in front of an armed trap; after Kalrag dies, move out of the spider corridor at once.
Carry an instant teleport and leave the Pass if HP is below 25 with no food left.

Iban's temple gate: enter the temple only at full HP (48/48), and run in without stopping (the wiki's own advice is to run in with plenty of health). Protect from Melee does not block the spikes. After any spike stun that returns you to the entrance, step back, eat to full and only then try again; never retry below full HP.

preconditions.food: 15+ food healing 12+ each (more is better; no bank beyond the Pass), with at least 6 left before the temple
required_items: Ranged weapon and ammunition for safespots
stop_conditions: Never jump a bridge below 40 HP
Never enter Iban's temple below 48/48 HP; after any spike stun, eat back to full before re-entering
If the spikes stun you back to the entrance twice in a row, or fewer than 6 food remain before the temple, teleport out and restock
Teleport out if HP < 25 and food is gone
Stop if more than three monsters are attacking at once
Dismiss any random event in the Pass; never accept one here

risk.bailout: Break the instant teleport (it works anywhere in the Pass). If stunned after Kalrag among spiders, eat first, then teleport. steps.rationale: 2,812.4 Agility XP plus 2,812.4 Defence XP that cannot be declined (F-2038): this is exactly the quest-sourced Defence the owner's zerker plan wants, taking Defence from 1 to 16 (tools/xp.py), far under the 50 cap. No hard skill requirements if the lyre is taken as a drop from the level 48 citizens (max hit 6, non-aggressive, F-5383). Fights: Draugen (max 7) and Koschei (max 3/5/7, then 1); only Koschei's 4th form is a safe death on Hardcore Worlds (F-0004/F-3014), forms 1-3 are run-ending. Placed in the 57 quest block so its Agility XP lands during the slowest training, and so the enchanted lyre (Rellekka teleport, F-4086) is ready when Rellekka opens at 80. Duel prep (risk.json S12): no ring of life at Koschei (it sends you to your respawn point and restarts the fight at form 1, so worn into form 4 it resets the fight every time; F-5011), and BANK the escape crystal before the duel: do not take it into the instance, worn or carried (worn, it resets the fight the same way; carried, it can fire if you stand still in the fourth form and restart the fight at form 1; risk.json S12-M6). Carry it only for the road, the Draugen and the citizens. Neither the ring nor the crystal is an exit from forms 1-3.

prose.summary: Koschei's first three forms are run-ending with no documented exit; only the fourth is a safe death. Gives {{step.xp_gained}} Agility XP, quest Defence, the lyre.
instructions: Bank for the road trips: food, Camelot teleport tablets (at least two per trip), and Ranged weapon and ammunition.
Gear: Ranged on Rapid or Accurate, never Longrange; Longrange gives Defence XP.
Before the lyre: Camelot tablet, then the road north, left at the first fork. Stay on the road, skip the log balance north of Sinclair Mansion, fight nothing.
Do: farm the lyre from the non-aggressive citizens using the fire safespots with Ranged.
Do: fight the Draugen only during the hunt, at full HP with food.
Before the duel, bank your escape crystal and any ring of life. Take a full inventory of monkfish ({{fact:F-4062}} each) and an antipoison; no weapons, armour or runes.
Before the duel: cure any poison, check your connection is stable, and be at full HP ({{risk.min_hitpoints}}).
Do, first three forms: start each form at full HP, eat at the card's eat line, and trap Koschei across the floor hole or by the fire pillars to eat.
Do, fourth form: do not resist. Let him wear you down until the fight ends; this form is the safe phase.
Stop: when the quest completes. Keep the enchanted lyre charged for Rellekka.
warnings: Headline {{risk.inherent_ds}}, with prep {{risk.residual_ds}} ({{risk.tier}}). Highest with-prep score on the Balanced route. The first three forms have no documented exit, and a disconnect in the second or third is likely fatal.
Mandatory: bank the escape crystal before the duel. Worn, it acts like a ring of life and resets the fight to the first form; carried, it can fire if you stand still in the fourth.
Never wear a ring of life in the duel. It sends you to your respawn point and restarts the fight at the first form; it is not an exit.
Mandatory: start every form at full HP ({{risk.min_hitpoints}}), eat at the card's eat line, and trap Koschei whenever you need to eat and regenerate.
Stop condition: in the first three forms, if food falls to the card's reserve line, trap Koschei and stall. He eventually vanishes and the fight restarts: a time cost, not a death.
Mandatory: start the duel only on a stable connection and never below full HP. A disconnect leaves you in combat for up to a minute.
Camelot road before the lyre: travel at full HP with food and tablets. Walk on through chip damage; teleport at once at the card's road line or if two attackers engage.
If the Draugen engages outside the hunt, teleport away. Stop condition: leave Rellekka if HP falls to the card's Draugen line during the fight.
Stop condition: dismiss every random event. A death inside one is official on Hardcore Worlds.
This card changed since you first accepted it: no ring of life, no exit in the first three forms, and an unresearched road. Read it again before decision point `DP08` option B.
tips: Worth it for Agility XP, quest Defence far under your cap (watch the cap bar), and the lyre teleport that skips the long Camelot road.
Safer alternative: decision point `DP08` option A, staying on Pollnivneach with no Fremennik Trials.

hazards.description: Koschei duel in an instance under Thorvald's house with no armour, weapons or spells: forms 1-3 hit up to 3/5/7 every 4 ticks (2.4 s) and a death in any of them is run-ending on Hardcore Worlds (safe for HCIM, not here); form 4 hits 1 every tick, drains prayer, and is the only safe phase (the fight ends at 1 HP).

NO ring of life and NO worn escape crystal: a ring of life sends you to your respawn point and restarts the fight at form 1, so a ring worn into form 4 resets the fight every time and the quest can never be finished; every retry re-exposes you to forms 1-3. A worn escape crystal acts like a ring of life. The ring is therefore not an exit; walking or teleporting out mid-fight is undocumented. The only documented de-escalation is trapping Koschei (floor hole, fire pillars) to eat and regenerate; 10 minutes in one phase makes him disappear and the fight restart at form 1.
Draugen (69, max 7, aggressive, crush) roams the open Fremennik Province; the quest makes you cross the province several times at Defence 1.
Lyre farmed from level 48 citizens (max 6, non-aggressive, safespottable with Ranged at the fires).

Travel: before the lyre exists, the only route the owner has is a Camelot tablet and a long run north on the road (left at the first fork). The NPCs along that road and the Sinclair log balance's fail damage are UNRESEARCHED; every early trip of the quest uses this road.
Forced 2,812.4 Defence XP (Defence 1 to 16, under the cap of 50).

lethality.rationale: Raised from 3 to rate the travel conservatively: every early trip crosses the Camelot-to-Rellekka road, whose NPCs were never researched (F-5343), at Defence 1. The known hazards alone are lower: Koschei form 3 and the Draugen hit up to 7 (15% of 48 HP) every 2.4 s with no armour; form 4 deals up to 100 per minute but ends the fight at 1 HP.

pvp.rationale: Kandarin and the Fremennik Province; no Wilderness.

escape.rationale: Raised from 4 now that the ring of life is removed: the duel is an instance with no documented exit (walking or teleporting out mid-fight is undocumented, F-5011); a ring of life or worn escape crystal only resets the fight to form 1 (F-5011, F-0015). Rated as a locked fight with no exit.

attention.rationale: No weapons: trapping and flinching Koschei, eating, timing each form.

disconnect.rationale: A disconnect in forms 2-3 leaves you up to 60 s taking max-5/7 hits every 2.4 s at Defence 1 with no armour: likely fatal. The escape crystal's scope inside this instance is undocumented, so it earns no credit.

unpredictability.rationale: Several fights; the 10-minute reset; lyre drop RNG; a roaming aggressive Draugen and unresearched road NPCs.

exposure.rationale: Long quest with lyre farming and several road trips: a few hours.

knowledge.rationale: Form 1-3 max hits are single-page; mid-fight exit undocumented; the Hardcore Worlds form-4 safe exception is under 30 days old; the road north is unresearched (kept at 4 until the road RFI is answered).

hw_death_classification.note: Only a loss in Koschei's 4th form is a safe death on Hardcore Worlds (F-5002/F-3014); every other death in the quest, including Koschei forms 1-3 (safe for HCIM, not here), the Draugen, the citizens and anything on the road, is official and run-ending. A death in form 4 caused by poison or anything else carried into the fight is not covered (F-5002 caveat). Classified UNSAFE_DEATH for the step.

mitigations.action: Remove any ring of life and do NOT wear the escape crystal before entering the Koschei instance. The wiki says a ring of life teleports you to your respawn point and you must fight him again from form 1; worn into form 4 it would reset the fight every time, so the quest could never be finished. A worn escape crystal acts like a ring of life. Neither is an exit.

Bring a full inventory of the best food you can buy (16 per piece, monkfish, is the largest verified heal); cure any poison before entering; start every form at 48/48 HP; eat whenever HP is 30 or lower (more than four form-3 max hits); trap Koschei across the floor hole or by the fire pillars to eat and regenerate.
Farm the lyre from the non-aggressive level 48 citizens using the fire safespots with Ranged; fight the Draugen at full HP with food.

Camelot road (first trips, before the lyre): travel at 48/48 HP with food and at least two Camelot tablets; stay on the road (left at the first fork) and do not attempt the log balance north of Sinclair Mansion; do not fight anything that attacks you on the road: walk on if it is chip damage, but teleport away at once if HP falls below 35 or if two attackers engage, and report what attacked you so the road can be rated. If the Draugen engages outside the hunt (it is aggressive and roams the province), teleport away rather than fight it unprepared. Watch for: aggressive NPCs of any kind (unresearched), the roaming Draugen (max 7), and the log balance (can be failed, damage unresearched). No factor credit: the road's hazards are unresearched.
Start the duel only on a stable connection, and never start a form below full HP: a disconnect leaves you in combat for up to 60 s.

Escape crystal (not credited): BANK it before the Koschei duel; do not take it into the instance, worn or carried. Worn, it acts like a ring of life (F-0015) and resets the fight to form 1 (F-5011). Carried, it fires when you take damage after its set inactivity time (2-300 s, F-3017); form 4 hits 1 every tick (F-5009), so if you stand still in the fourth form it can fire, teleport you out and restart the fight at form one (F-0015, F-5011), back through the run-ending forms 1-3. Its scope inside this instance is undocumented (F-5386) and it earns no credit in the duel, so banking it gives up no counted protection. For the rest of the quest (road, Draugen, citizens) carry it as the general escape-crystal rule says. Never wear a ring of life in the duel either (S12-M1).

preconditions.food: full inventory of 16-heal food (monkfish) for Koschei; food for the Draugen and the road trips
required_items: Ranged weapon and ammunition for the citizens and the Draugen (left outside the duel: weapons are not allowed)
at least two Camelot teleport tablets per road trip

stop_conditions: Never enter the Koschei instance wearing a ring of life, or with the escape crystal worn or in the inventory: bank the crystal first (worn, it resets the fight; carried, it can fire if you stand still in form 4 and restart the fight at form 1)
Never start a Koschei form below 48/48 HP; eat whenever HP is 30 or lower

On the Camelot road: teleport away if HP falls below 35 or two attackers engage; never fight on the road
Teleport away if the Draugen engages outside the hunt; fight it only at full HP with food
Leave Rellekka if HP < 30 during the Draugen fight
Dismiss any random event during the quest; never accept one on the road or in the province

risk.bailout: Duel (forms 1-3): there is no documented exit. Trap Koschei across the floor hole or by the fire pillars and eat back to full; if food is running out, keep him trapped until he disappears after 10 minutes in the phase and the fight restarts at form 1 (lowest-hitting form), then leave the instance the normal way between fights and restock. Try a teleport or walking out only as a last resort and never plan around it (undocumented). Never put on a ring of life (or the escape crystal) as an exit: it resets the fight and every retry is another pass through forms 1-3. Form 4: do not resist; let him take you to 1 HP, which ends the fight (the safe phase). Standing still here is safe only because the escape crystal is in the bank: carried, it can fire after its inactivity time and restart the fight at form 1; if you find it in your inventory anyway, keep walking until he brings you to 1 HP (it does not fire while you move). Road and province: break a Camelot tablet away from anything that attacks or from the Draugen outside the hunt, and come back at full HP.

The honest card: in forms 1-3 there is no exit, a death is run-ending, and the only control is food, full HP before each form, trapping Koschei and a stable connection; a disconnect in forms 2-3 is likely fatal and no verified mitigation covers it, so the DISCONNECT_FATAL floor holds the score with prep. Rellekka has no bank (F-4087); bring what you need. With The Fremennik Trials done (S12) the enchanted lyre teleports here (F-4086); otherwise a Camelot tablet and a long run north (F-5343).

steps.title: Troll Stronghold (2,000 Agility XP since 3 Nov 2026)
steps.rationale: 2,000 Agility XP added in Quest Month (F-0029). Required kills: Dad (101, max 27, safespot at the western gate, F-5017), one of several aggressive Troll generals (113, max 38: two hits exceed 48 HP, F-5018) and, at Thieving 24, Berry and Twig (71, max 13, safespot from a cell, F-5019). The owner's 57 Agility uses the rock shortcuts (41-47) that avoid the thrower trolls entirely (F-5376). Offered only as a decision-point option.

prose.summary: Aggressive Troll generals can kill from full HP in two hits. Prep brings it to {{risk.tier}}. Reward: {{fact:F-2022}} and the gate to Troll Romance.
instructions: Bank: a full inventory of monkfish ({{fact:F-4062}} each), prayer potions, a games necklace, and Ranged weapon and ammunition.
Gear: Ranged on Rapid or Accurate, never Longrange; Longrange gives Defence XP.
Travel: Trollheim by the rock shortcuts, which avoid the thrower trolls on the mountain path.
Do: fight Dad only from the western-gate safespot, with Ranged.
Do: turn Protect from Melee on before entering the generals' room, then kill only the southern-most general from the desk safespot with Ranged.
Do: fight Berry and Twig only from inside a vacant cell.
Do: leave by the secret exit to the south and teleport out.
Stop: at quest completion, or at any stop condition below.
warnings: Headline {{risk.inherent_ds}}, with prep {{risk.residual_ds}} ({{risk.tier}}). Optional for Agility alone; decision point `DP03` option A skips it. Worth it for the quest and the gate to Troll Romance.
Mandatory: never enter the generals' room without Protect from Melee on, full prayer and full HP ({{risk.min_hitpoints}}).
Mandatory: in the generals' room, eat whenever HP is at or below a general's maximum hit (the card's eat line). Below it, one hit can kill.
Stop conditions: leave if two generals attack; leave the room and teleport if food or prayer falls to the card's lines.
Never fight a general in melee range. Bail-out: keep Protect from Melee on, back away to the desk safespot or out of the room, and teleport.
Escape crystal: optional and not credited; its scope here is undocumented and it does not fire while you move. Never lower another precaution for it.

steps.title: Troll Romance
steps.rationale: 8,000 Agility XP (F-2032 also lists 4,000 Strength, not carried as a number). The required Arrg fight is the problem: level 113, 38 melee / 30 accurate ranged, occasionally through protection prayers, attacks the moment you arrive, and the wiki says it is not a safe death even for Hardcore Ironmen (F-2036/F-5021); on Hardcore Worlds it is run-ending (F-5003). Decision-point option only; not recommended at 48 Hitpoints. Prep card (risk.json S17): Protect from Melee on before talking to Arrg and during the run to the safespot (his primary attack is the 38 melee, F-5021/F-3089), Protect from Missiles only once at the safespot; the run to the safespot cannot be made fully safe (two hits can kill at 48 HP; it partly depends on hit RNG).

prose.summary: Arrg attacks on arrival and the run to the safespot cannot be made fully safe. Reward: {{fact:F-2031}} of Agility, saving almost no training time.
instructions: Bank: a full inventory of monkfish ({{fact:F-4062}} each), leaving room for prayer potions; Ranged weapon and ammunition.
Gear: Ranged on Rapid or Accurate, never Longrange; Longrange gives Defence XP.
Travel: Trollheim to the troll arena at full HP and full prayer, on a stable connection.
Do: turn Protect from Melee on before you talk to Arrg.
Do: run straight to the north-west wall or west-gate safespot without fighting. Eat one piece whenever HP reaches the card's run eat line and keep moving.
Do: at the safespot, switch to Protect from Missiles and fight with Ranged. Eat at the card's safespot line and keep prayer topped up.
Stop: when Arrg dies, or hold the safespot until he despawns if a stop condition is met.
warnings: The run window cannot be closed. With Protect from Melee on, two maximum ranged hits and one monkfish leave you almost dead from full HP; a third hit, or melee through the prayer, kills.
No verified food heals more, no combo-eating is verified, and the run's length is undocumented.
Headline {{risk.inherent_ds}}, with prep {{risk.residual_ds}} ({{risk.tier}}). Highest with-prep score in this plan. A death here is run-ending and not a safe death even for Hardcore Ironmen.
Stop condition before starting: do not start unless you accept that the run can kill a prepared player, or if Troll Stronghold showed you cannot hold a protection prayer and eat under fire.
Mandatory: talk to Arrg at full HP ({{risk.min_hitpoints}}), full prayer, Protect from Melee already on and a full inventory of monkfish-class food.
Mandatory: start only on a stable connection. A disconnect leaves you in combat for up to a minute, and during the run both his attacks can reach you.
Stop condition: if food or prayer falls to the card's lines at the safespot, stop attacking and hold it under Protect from Missiles until Arrg despawns; restock and return.
No bail-out during the run: keep moving and eat. Teleport in the arena is undocumented (last resort only), logging out is not an exit, and the escape crystal never fires while you move.
Stop condition: dismiss every random event. A death inside one is official on Hardcore Worlds.
tips: Reason to do it: Strength XP and quest completion. Optional for Agility; decision point `DP03` option A skips it.

hazards.description: Arrg (113, 140 HP): 'primarily' a moderately inaccurate 38 slash melee, plus a 'significantly' more accurate 30 ranged; attack speed 4 ticks; both occasionally hit through protection prayers; he attacks the moment you are teleported into the arena and you auto-retaliate.

The run from the arena centre to a safespot (north-west mountain wall / west gate, or the northern gate) is taken under fire from both attacks; the run's length in ticks is not documented, so the number of attacks you take is unbounded by any fact.
Not a safe death even for HCIM; run-ending on Hardcore Worlds. Whether a teleport works in the arena is not stated.

lethality.rationale: 38 is 79% and 30 is 62% of 48 HP; two attacks 4 ticks apart exceed 48 HP; both occasionally pass prayer.

escape.rationale: Arena reached by NPC transport; teleport behaviour mid-fight undocumented; the documented way out is holding a safespot until he despawns.

attention.rationale: Prayer choice and switch, safespot movement and eating under fire.

disconnect.rationale: A disconnect in the arena is likely fatal: 60 s in combat against 38/30 hits. The escape crystal does not fire while moving and its scope in the arena is undocumented, so no credit.

unpredictability.rationale: Through-prayer hits; two attack styles; RNG decides whether the run is survivable.

knowledge.rationale: Raised from 3: the survival-critical quantities are undocumented (run length in ticks, through-prayer frequency, arena teleport behaviour).

hw_death_classification.note: Explicitly not a safe death even for HCIM; run-ending on Hardcore Worlds.

mitigations.action: RUN PHASE: turn Protect from Melee on before talking to Arrg and keep it on during the run. His primary attack is the 38 melee, so the prayer blocks the heavier and more frequent style; the unblocked ranged hit is 30. Run straight to the north-west wall / west-gate safespot without stopping to fight.

SAFESPOT PHASE: once at the safespot, where his melee cannot reach, switch to Protect from Missiles and fight with Ranged. The only incoming attack is then the 30 rock, which passes the prayer only occasionally. Keep 20+ prayer points with prayer potions.

EAT RULES. Food: 16 heal per piece minimum (monkfish; 16 is the largest single heal in the verified facts). During the run: eat one piece at once whenever HP is 38 or lower (that is, after almost any hit) and keep moving. At the safespot: eat whenever HP is 34 or lower, so HP is always above 30 before the next rock.

HONEST LIMIT, print it in the guide: the run window cannot be closed with verified facts. With Protect from Melee on, two max ranged hits with one 16-heal between them take you 48 -> 18 -> 34 -> 4; a third max hit before the safespot, or any through-prayer 38 after the first hit, kills. A 38 from 48 leaves 10, and 10 + 16 = 26 is below the next 30. No verified food heals more than 16 and no verified fact covers combo-eating (e.g. karambwan) or eating speed, so no combo-eat rule can be given. Surviving the run depends on Arrg's hit rolls and on the run being short, and its length is undocumented.
Start only on a stable connection: a disconnect leaves you in combat for up to 60 s, and the run is the phase where both attacks can reach you.

Escape crystal (not credited, optional): carry it set to a short inactivity timer. It does not fire while you move, so it cannot cover the run; standing at the safespot it might fire if you disconnect, but whether it works in the Troll arena is undocumented.

During the run there is no bail-out: keep moving to the safespot and eat at 38 or lower. Whether a teleport works in the arena is undocumented (RFI), so try one only as a last resort and never plan around it. Stated plainly: the run window CANNOT be closed with verified facts. Two ranged max hits with one eat leave 4 HP, and any through-prayer 38 after the first hit kills; there is no verified combo-eat. Whether the run is survived depends on hit RNG. Extreme unmitigated and still High with prep, the highest with-prep score of any plan step. Defence cap: the Sins of the Father chain forces 4,600 Defence XP (Defence 24 with The Fremennik Trials); put no lamp or tome from the chain into Defence.

hallowed crystal shards or vyre noble robes
stop_conditions: Do not enter below 70 Hitpoints

Practise floors 1-3 before floor 4
Dismiss any random event in Darkmeyer or the Sepulchre; never accept one here

risk.bailout: Traps damage you when you run into them and send you back to just before them (F-3057): stop on a tile clear of traps, eat to full, then continue. In Darkmeyer, wear vyre noble robes or arrive by crystal shard so the Vyrewatch (max 17) stay passive.

necessity.why: Highest Agility XP rates for 77-99 (73,000-81,000 XP/h to floor 4, more on floor 5) against 66,000-70,184 on Ardougne, but no marks of grace, and only after Sins of the Father.

risk.verdict_reason: Long-term goal only (DP07 option B). Severe unmitigated at the owner's 48 HP: undocumented trap damage (UNVERIFIED_MECHANIC floor), tick-precise floors and the bulk of the grind. decision_points.question: Which course for 57 to 60, before Seers' opens at 60?

options.title: Falador Rooftop Course
options.justification: About twice Canifis's XP rate (27,200-35,000 vs 14,000-19,700 XP/h) with small, documented failure damage (3-8 on the Hand Holds until 66).
pros: Fail damage known and small against 48 HP
City course, no aggressive monsters noted
cons: Fails until 66
Fewer marks than Canifis (9.7-12.1/h)
options.profit_note: Falador earns the fewest marks per hour (low end 9.7/h) but reaches Seers' sooner.

options.title: Canifis Rooftop Course
options.justification: Best marks of grace per hour of the low courses (16-18/h, never penalised), so it starts the Graceful set early, but at roughly half the XP rate.
pros: Bank at the course, free Ectophial teleport nearby
Only one failable gap, stops failing at 64
cons: About half Falador's XP/h
Failure damage not documented
options.best_for: Owners who want Graceful before Seers'
options.profit_note: Canifis earns more marks per hour (low end 16/h) but at about half the XP rate; marks sell as amylase crystals on the HW GE.

decision_points.recommendation_reason: Only three levels remain before Seers'; Falador gets there far sooner with a known, small damage source. Graceful marks come later at Seers', Pollnivneach and Ardougne.

decision_points.question: Do the reachable Agility-XP quests now, and which ones?
decision_points.conditions: Every option here gives 0 Defence XP except The Fremennik Trials (2,812.4, Defence 1 to 16), which stays far under the cap of 50.

options.title: Only the no-combat / trivial-combat quests (The Writing's on the Wall, The Depths of Despair)
options.justification: 4,000 fixed Agility XP with no documented damage source except a max-hit-3 snake; the Thieving XP also moves Thieving toward Death on the Isle's 34.
cons: Leaves the bigger Regicide reward (13,750) for later
options.profit_note: No direct profit: quest steps carry none (marks come from the rooftop laps that follow).

options.title: Full reachable quest block (A + Icthlarin's Little Helper, A Tail of Two Cats, Underground Pass, Regicide, The Fremennik Trials)
options.justification: All fixed or lamp Agility XP the owner can reach today, plus quest-sourced Defence for the zerker. Every required fight is safespottable or blocked by protection prayers, and the XP lands where training is slowest (Falador, 57-60).
pros: Adds the 4,000 + 5,000 (lamps) + 3,000 + 13,750 + 2,812.4 Agility XP of the cited rewards; combined effect is in the calculator output
Quest Defence (Defence 16) from The Fremennik Trials, per the owner's zerker plan
Regicide unlocks Tirannwn; the lyre teleports to Rellekka at 80
cons: Hours of questing that the calculator does not count (no verified quest durations)

Underground Pass traps up to 24 and spider pile-ups; Icthlarin flashbacks block teleports; Koschei forms 1-3 are not safe deaths (never wear a ring of life in the duel, and bank the escape crystal before it: worn, it resets the fight; carried, it can fire if you stand still in the fourth form)
options.best_for: The balanced route and the owner's quest-based zerker build
options.profit_note: No direct profit: quest steps carry none (marks come from the rooftop laps that follow).

options.title: Skip quests for now; rooftops only
options.justification: Training alone has the simplest danger profile; the quests stay available and can be done at any level because their XP is fixed.
cons: Fixed XP is worth more time now (slowest training) than later
No quest Defence progress
options.profit_note: Rooftop income at the low end of the mark range: Falador Rooftop Course 9.7 marks/h; marks are converted to amylase crystals and sold on the HW GE.

decision_points.recommendation_reason: The owner optimises for balance and builds Defence only through quests; option B gives the most fixed XP where it saves the most training time, with fights that can all be safespotted or prayed against. Underground Pass and Regicide carry full prep cards (risk.json) and the owner has already accepted both; choose A for the lowest-danger quest set.

decision_points.question: Do the Troll quests (Death Plateau, Troll Stronghold, Troll Romance)?
decision_points.conditions: The owner's 57 Agility already uses the Trollheim rock shortcuts (41-47) that avoid the multi-combat thrower trolls.

options.title: Skip the Troll quests for now; keep training
options.justification: The required fights hit 27-38 (Dad, Troll generals, Arrg) against 48 Hitpoints for only 2,000 + 8,000 Agility XP of fixed rewards.
pros: Avoids the two most dangerous fights in the quest list
cons: Leaves 10,000 fixed Agility XP, 4,000 Strength XP and three quest completions unclaimed for now
options.profit_note: Rooftop income at the low end of the mark range: Seers' Village Rooftop Course 11 marks/h; marks are converted to amylase crystals and sold on the HW GE.

options.title: Death Plateau and Troll Stronghold only
options.justification: 2,000 Agility XP (new in Quest Month); Dad and the southern-most Troll general can be safespotted with Ranged, and Berry/Twig from a cell.
pros: Safespots documented for every required kill
Thrower trolls avoided by the 57-Agility shortcuts
cons: Several aggressive Troll generals (max 38) share the room; two hits exceed 48 HP
Only 2,000 Agility XP
options.best_for: Owners who want the quest points and unlock now
options.profit_note: No direct profit: quest steps carry none (marks come from the rooftop laps that follow).

options.title: All three, including Troll Romance
options.justification: Adds 8,000 Agility XP and 4,000 Strength XP from Troll Romance (F-2031, F-2032). Allowed under the informed policy: the Risk Officer approves it with conditions and a full prep card. Arrg is aggressive on arrival, hits up to 38 melee / 30 ranged, occasionally through protection prayers, and is not a safe death (F-2036, F-5021, F-5003); the run from the arena centre to the safespot is the one window where two unblocked hits can exceed 48 HP (risk.json).
pros: 4,000 Strength XP and the quest completion

Documented safespots and a prep card (48/48 HP, full prayer, Protect from Melee on before talking to Arrg and kept on during the run, because his primary attack is the 38 melee; switch to Protect from Missiles only at the safespot; F-5021, risk.json S17-M1/M2)
cons: Arrg is the most dangerous required fight in this plan (F-5003)
Not a safe death even for Hardcore Ironmen
For the Agility goal alone, 8,000 XP saves less time than the quest takes (risk.json necessity: optional)
The run to the safespot cannot be made fully safe (two hits can kill at 48 HP; it partly depends on hit RNG) (risk.json S17-M4)
options.best_for: Owners who want the Troll quests and the Strength XP, after Troll Stronghold has shown they can hold a protection prayer and eat under fire
options.profit_note: No direct profit: quest steps carry none (marks come from the rooftop laps that follow).

decision_points.recommendation_reason: For the Agility goal alone the Troll rewards are small next to the fights, so A is recommended. B and C are allowed under the informed policy with their prep cards (the owner already accepted Troll Stronghold); choose C if the quest completions and Troll Romance's 4,000 Strength XP matter to you, and do B first so the Troll Stronghold fights test your prayer and eating under fire before Arrg.

decision_points.question: Small or gated quest detours: Recruitment Drive chain, or train Thieving to 34 for Death on the Isle?

options.title: Skip both for now
options.justification: Recruitment Drive needs two extra quests for 1,000.5 Agility XP; Death on the Isle needs ten more Thieving levels first.
cons: Leaves the 1,000.5 and 7,500 Agility XP rewards unclaimed for now
options.profit_note: Rooftop income at the low end of the mark range: Falador Rooftop Course 9.7 marks/h; marks are converted to amylase crystals and sold on the HW GE.

options.title: Druidic Ritual, Black Knights' Fortress, Recruitment Drive
options.justification: Clears three quests and gives 1,000.5 Agility XP plus two 1,000 XP combat lamps (never into Defence).
cons: Sir Leye is fought with no armour or food and is not a safe death
Very little Agility XP for the time
options.best_for: Owners clearing the quest list anyway
options.profit_note: No direct profit: quest steps carry none (marks come from the rooftop laps that follow).

options.title: Train Thieving to 34, then Death on the Isle
options.justification: 7,500 Agility XP plus Thieving and Crafting XP, and the wiki says its two fights cannot kill; the cost is Thieving training the plan cannot size from verified facts.
pros: Fights scripted to stop before death (wiki)
cons: Thieving 34 needed (owner 24, at least 26 after The Writing's on the Wall)
Fights with no food or teleports; no Hardcore Worlds safe exception
options.profit_note: No direct profit: quest steps carry none (marks come from the rooftop laps that follow).

decision_points.recommendation_reason: Neither detour is efficient for Agility now. Take option C if Thieving reaches 34 through other play; take B only when clearing quests for their own sake.

decision_points.question: At 70: move to Pollnivneach or stay on Seers'?

options.justification: Faster (47,000-51,000 XP/h), only the market stall can fail (4 damage at 48 HP) and nothing fails from 85.
cons: Carpet travel from Shantay Pass; never walk south of town (crocodiles)
Pollnivneach tablets need an NMZ scroll (NMZ is unsafe on Hardcore Worlds)

options.profit_note: Rooftop income at the low end of the mark range: Pollnivneach Rooftop Course 13 marks/h; marks are converted to amylase crystals and sold on the HW GE.

options.title: Stay on Seers' to 80
options.justification: Familiar course with the bank at the start; fails stop at 79.
cons: Slower (planned 40,000 XP/h)
Marks drop to 20% at 80
options.profit_note: Rooftop income at the low end of the mark range: Seers' Village Rooftop Course 11 marks/h; marks are converted to amylase crystals and sold on the HW GE.

decision_points.recommendation_reason: Pollnivneach is faster and its only failable obstacle has a known 4-damage hit, so it is at least as safe as Seers'.

decision_points.question: Work toward the Hallowed Sepulchre (Sins of the Father), or stay on rooftops?
decision_points.conditions: Floor 4 needs 77 and Floor 5 87 since 12 Aug 2026 (boostable). Sins of the Father needs Woodcutting 62, Fletching 60, Crafting 56, Slayer 50, Attack 50 and Magic 49 plus five quests.

options.title: Stay on rooftops (Pollnivneach / Rellekka, then Ardougne)
options.justification: Reachable now, low failure damage, marks of grace for Graceful.
cons: Lower XP/h than the Sepulchre (47,000-66,000 vs 73,000+)
options.profit_note: Rooftop income at the low end of the mark range: Pollnivneach Rooftop Course 13 marks/h, Rellekka Rooftop Course 13 marks/h, Ardougne Rooftop Course 16 marks/h; marks are converted to amylase crystals and sold on the HW GE.

options.title: LONG-TERM goal: Hallowed Sepulchre runs to Floor 4 (after Sins of the Father)
options.justification: 73,000-81,000 XP/h to Floor 4 from 77 (F-1058), the highest rate in this range, and Sins of the Father's tome (6 x 15,000 XP) can all go to Agility (F-2102). A long-term goal, not a choice for today. Preconditions: (1) Sins of the Father researched and completed: the Sepulchre needs it (F-1054), and the quest needs Woodcutting 62, Fletching 60, Crafting 56, Attack 50, Slayer 50 and Magic 49 plus A Taste of Hope and its chain (F-2100, F-2101). Sins of the Father (former S24) is pending research: it is vetoed for insufficient facts to prepare (its fights' max hits and teleport rules are unresearched) and lifts when its fights are researched as the owner nears the requirements. (2) 70+ Hitpoints recommended for the traps (F-3056; owner 48). The Sepulchre itself is approved with conditions. (3) Defence cap: the Sins of the Father prerequisite chain gives 4,600 forced Defence XP (Nature Spirit 2,000, In Search of the Myreque 600, In Aid of the Myreque 2,000; F-2101, F-2132); with The Fremennik Trials (2,812.4, F-2038) that is Defence about 24 (7,412.4 XP, tools/xp.py), under the cap of 50. No tome or lamp in the chain may go to Defence.
pros: Highest Agility XP/h available in the 77-99 range
Sins of the Father's tome adds 90,000 Agility XP (F-2102)
cons: Not reachable now: six skills, five quests and the Sins of the Father research come first
Trap damage undocumented; 70+ HP recommended (owner 48)
Darkmeyer Vyrewatch (max 17 without vyre noble robes); no marks of grace
Forced Defence XP: the Sins of the Father chain adds 4,600 Defence XP (Defence about 24 with The Fremennik Trials; cap 50)
options.best_for: The owner's long-term next step once the account's other skills near Sins of the Father's requirements
options.profit_note: Rooftop steps earn marks of grace, sold as amylase crystals on the HW GE (see each step's income); quest steps carry no profit.

decision_points.recommendation_reason: Option A is what this account can do today. Keep option B as the long-term goal: when Woodcutting, Fletching, Crafting, Attack, Slayer and Magic near Sins of the Father's requirements, ask for its fights to be researched (this lifts the veto), complete it, reach 70+ Hitpoints, then move to the Sepulchre from 77.

decision_points.question: At 80: Rellekka or stay on Pollnivneach?

options.title: Stay on Pollnivneach to 90
options.justification: Nothing can fail from 85, so the last five levels before Ardougne have no damage source on the course; known travel.
cons: Marks fall to 20% at 90
options.profit_note: Rooftop income at the low end of the mark range: Pollnivneach Rooftop Course 13 marks/h; marks are converted to amylase crystals and sold on the HW GE.

options.title: The Fremennik Trials (if not done) and Rellekka
options.justification: Higher XP/h and marks; the tightrope fails only until 85 for 4 damage; the quest gives the owner quest-sourced Defence and the lyre teleport.
pros: Quest Defence 2,812.4 and the enchanted lyre
cons: No bank in Rellekka
Route from Camelot partly unresearched

Koschei forms 1-3 are not safe deaths (never wear a ring of life in the duel, and bank the escape crystal before it: worn, it resets the fight; carried, it can fire if you stand still in the fourth form)
options.profit_note: Rooftop income at the low end of the mark range: Rellekka Rooftop Course 13 marks/h; marks are converted to amylase crystals and sold on the HW GE.

decision_points.recommendation_reason: For the owner's balanced goal Rellekka is the faster course with the same small fail damage, and The Fremennik Trials doubles as quest Defence for the zerker. Choose A for the lowest-danger finish.

facts.statement: Post-12-August-2026 Wyrm XP per lap is unconfirmed. The course page (flagged {{Obsolete}} for the 12 Aug 2026 changes) states 633 basic / 1,053.6 advanced, but its own basic obstacle table sums to 601.6 (7 x 37.2 + 341.2); the advanced table sums to 1,053.6. The Agility skill page still gives the pre-rework 504.1 / 749.6. Jagex's T1 notes give no per-lap numbers.

facts.statement: The Fremennik Trials requires fighting Koschei the deathless in an instance with no armour, weapons or spells. Food, prayer, god books and jewellery are allowed. His four forms have 30/50/70/255 HP and max hits of 3/5/7/1. The wiki says dying to any form is safe for regular hardcore ironmen, but that hardcore group ironmen must be concerned about dying in the first three forms. Hardcore Worlds uses the HGIM death ruleset, so forms 1-3 must be treated as potentially run-ending. The 4th-form death is scripted.
facts.caveat: Resolves the researcher's doubt: the 4th-form max hit of 1 is not an anomaly. That form attacks every game tick (0.6 s) for exactly 1, drains prayer, and has 255 HP. The third form has a 10-minute time limit. A ring of life sends you back to spawn and resets him to form 1. If he stays idle too long he resets to form 1. On HW, death safety for forms 1-3 needs a Threat-desk ruling (RFI-01 already open).

sources.title: Koschei the deathless
sources.quote: Dying to any of his forms are safe deaths (including for [[Hardcore ironmen]]), though players must die to his fourth form (or defeat it) to get the vote. Only [[Hardcore group ironmen]] need to be concerned about dying to the first three forms, as dying to the fourth form is a scripted safe death.

facts.statement: Monkey Madness I's only Defence XP comes from Daero's optional training after the quest: 35,000 to Attack and Defence and 20,000 to Strength and Hitpoints, or the reverse. Since 30 November 2022 you can return to Ape Atoll without accepting the training. A zerker can therefore take 0 Defence XP. If the training is accepted, Defence gets at least 20,000 (35,000 = level 39 by tools/xp.py).
facts.caveat: Build-critical: the route must say to decline (ignore) Daero's training. Declining means heavy ballistae cannot be used later, which does not affect Agility. Confirmed by a Jagex T1 post.

sources.title: Monkey Madness I
sources.quote: '''Note:''' while it was previously impossible to return to Ape Atoll after quest completion without receiving experience from Daero, an [[Update:The Garden of Death & More#Poll 77 Changes|update]] in November 2022 now allows the training to be ignored before returning.

sources.title: Update:The Garden of Death & More
sources.quote: '''Poll 77 Changes''' * Players can now get back to Ape Atoll without accepting Daero's Training, after completing Monkey Madness I.

facts.subject: Werewolf Agility Course
facts.value: can hit over 30 damage
facts.statement: On the Werewolf Agility Course the deathslide is the only obstacle that can be failed. A fall can deal over 30 damage, which does not scale with Hitpoints, and it is the only Agility obstacle that can deal damage past the player's Hitpoints. Higher Agility and Strength and lower weight improve success; with Agility and Strength 80+ and weight 2 kg or less it never fails.
facts.caveat: Danger-critical for a 48-HP Hardcore Worlds character: a deathslide fail can kill. The owner's Strength is 32 (far from 80). No head-slot item may be worn on the deathslide. The Threat desk must rate this before routing.

facts.subject: Seers' Village Rooftop Course
facts.statement: A perfect Seers' rooftop lap takes 73 ticks (43.8 s), giving at most about 46,600 XP/h (~81 laps); with the Seers' bank teleport (about 37 s per lap) the maximum is about 56,000 XP/h (~97 laps). Each lap gives 570 XP.

facts.statement: The escape crystal does not activate while the player is moving. If the inactivity time is reached mid-movement, it fires only when the player stops.

facts.subject: Disconnect during combat
facts.statement: If a player disconnects unexpectedly while in combat, the character stays in the game for up to 60 seconds and can keep taking hits before it is logged out.

sources.title: Logout button
sources.quote: This works because of a 60 second timer before the game forcibly logs you out after an unexpected disconnection during combat. To use this effectively, you need to survive 60 seconds of combat while disconnected.

facts.subject: Logout in combat
facts.statement: A player cannot log out until 16 ticks (9.6 seconds) after they last received a hit.

sources.title: Logout button
sources.quote: players in [[combat]] cannot log out until 16 game [[Game tick|ticks]], or 9.6 seconds, after they have last received a hit.

facts.subject: Wilderness Agility Course
facts.value: x-logging does not work in singles-plus combat
facts.statement: X-logging (closing the client to escape a PKer) does not work in singles-plus combat areas, and the Wilderness Agility Course is one of them.

sources.title: Logout button
sources.quote: X-logging is done to escape a potential [[PvP]] scenario in [[Single-way combat]]; this will not work in [[Singles-plus combat]].

sources.title: Singles-plus combat
sources.quote: Currently, the only singles-plus combat areas are: * the [[Revenant Caves]] * the [[Wilderness Agility Course]]

facts.subject: Owner's character (brief stats)
facts.statement: My own recomputation from the brief's stats (Def 1, HP 48, Prayer 44, Atk 44, Str 32, Ranged 56, Magic 44) gives base = (1+48+22)/4 = 17.75. Ranged = 0.325 x floor(56 x 1.5) = 0.325 x 84 = 27.3, melee = 0.325 x 76 = 24.7, magic = 0.325 x 66 = 21.45. Combat = floor(17.75 + 27.3) = floor(45.05) = 45. This matches the Director's correction (ledger seq 49).

sources.title: Combat level
sources.quote: \text{Final} &= \lfloor \text{Base} + \textrm{max}(\text{Melee}, \text{Range}, \text{Mage}) \rfloor

facts.subject: Level-based monster aggression
facts.value: aggressive if player combat level <= 2 x monster level; vs combat 45 every level-based aggressive monster of level 23+ attacks
facts.statement: Level-based aggressive monsters attack players whose combat level is at most twice their own. At combat 45 (the Director's figure), any such monster of level 23 or higher attacks (2 x 23 = 46 >= 45; 2 x 22 = 44 < 45). Monsters of level 63+ attack every player.

sources.title: Aggressiveness
sources.quote: When aggressiveness is based on combat level, an aggressive monster will attack a player whose combat level is less than or equal to twice the monster's level.

facts.subject: Kharidian Desert (Agility Pyramid, desert travel)
facts.statement: Outside towns, desert heat deals 1-10 damage every 24-132 seconds (90 by default; armour shortens it) unless a waterskin dose is drunk. Towns such as Pollnivneach, and open dialogue boxes, are exempt. The 90 s base is backed by a cited Jagex Mod Ash statement (150 ticks).

sources.title: Desert heat
sources.quote: For every 24-132 seconds (depending on armour worn) that a player spends in the desert, they will take 1-10 damage. [...] Players are not affected by desert heat while they are within the boundaries of towns or while a dialogue box is open. The default interval between damage is 90 seconds.

facts.subject: Hallowed Sepulchre
facts.statement: The wiki recommends 70+ Hitpoints to withstand trap damage. The owner has 48.

sources.title: Hallowed Sepulchre
sources.quote: * (Recommended) {{SCP|Hitpoints|70+|link=yes}} to withstand damage from traps.

facts.subject: Hallowed Sepulchre
facts.value: small per trap hit, per-floor values not documented
facts.statement: Running into a trap usually teleports the player back to just before it and deals 'a small amount of damage' unless a hallowed ring is worn. The traps are wizard-statue fire, knight-statue swords and crossbowman-statue bolts. The wiki says deeper floors' traps are faster or doubled, but gives no damage numbers.
facts.caveat: No damage figure exists on the pinned wiki pages, and a web search found none on other sources. Planners must not invent numbers. Use the 70 HP recommendation (F-3056) as the only guidance.

sources.title: Hallowed Sepulchre
sources.quote: In most cases, running into a trap will teleport the player to a location just before the trap on the path, costing the player time. This deals a small amount of damage unless the [[hallowed ring]] is equipped.

facts.value: lightning stuns briefly, leaving the player open to other traps
facts.statement: Priest statues summon lightning in a 3x3 chequerboard that briefly stuns the player instead of dealing damage, leaving them immobile and open to other traps.

sources.title: Hallowed Sepulchre

facts.subject: Hallowed Sepulchre: coffins
facts.value: failing to loot a coffin poisons the player (2-damage poison per Strategies)
facts.statement: A failed coffin loot (66 Thieving, boostable) poisons the player. A lockpick, or better the strange old lockpick, lowers the failure chance.
facts.caveat: The 2-damage figure is an inference. The Coffin page gives no poison strength, and the Strategies page mentions '2-damage poison' only in a footnote about curing with a prayer book; it does not state the coffin poison's starting damage. Bring antipoison regardless.

facts.subject: Hallowed ring
facts.value: negates all Sepulchre trap damage; 250 hallowed marks
facts.statement: The hallowed ring (250 hallowed marks from the Mysterious Hallowed Goods shop) negates all damage from failing environmental obstacles in the Sepulchre, such as knight-statue swords and crossbowman-statue bolts.
facts.caveat: It does not negate damage from failing to enchant portal frames (a coffin skilling challenge). It also has no effect on failing grapple pillars.

When equipped, it negates all damage taken from failing environmental obstacles [...] It has no effect on the recovery time for failing the grapple [[Pillar (Hallowed Sepulchre)|pillars]] and does not negate damage taken for failing to enchant [[Portal frame|portal frames]].

facts.subject: Werewolf Agility Course: deathslide
facts.value: upwards of 30 damage, does not scale with Hitpoints; can exceed current HP
facts.statement: A deathslide fall can deal over 30 damage. It does not scale with HP, and the deathslide is the only Agility obstacle that can deal damage past the player's current HP, so a fall can kill.
facts.caveat: The exact maximum is not documented: the wiki says only 'upwards of 30' and 'over 30', and the zip line page (rev 15333943) gives no figure. Do not assume that more than 30 HP is safe. Treat every attempt as potentially lethal for a 48 HP character until a maximum is sourced. No T1/T3 second source was found (a web search turned up T4 sites only).

sources.title: Werewolf Agility Course

facts.subject: Werewolf Agility Course: deathslide
facts.value: never fails with Agility 80, Strength 80 and weight <= 2 kg; success also depends on weight (best at 0 kg); no head-slot item allowed
facts.statement: Deathslide success depends on Agility, Strength and weight (best at 0 kg or below). It never fails at 80 Agility, 80 Strength and 2 kg or less, which the owner (Strength 32) is far from. No head-slot item may be worn.
facts.caveat: The Jagex quote cited on the page says 'over 80' and 'under 2kg', while the wiki text says '80' and '2 kg or lower'. Use the stricter reading (81+ and below 2 kg) for guaranteed success.

sources.title: Werewolf Agility Course

facts.subject: Pollnivneach Rooftop Course: market stall
facts.statement: The market stall is the only failable obstacle at Pollnivneach. A fall deals floor(current HP/17 + 2) damage, which is 4 at 48 HP (floor(4.82)). The course page says no part can be failed from 85 Agility.
facts.caveat: At 2 or fewer current HP the formula gives 2 damage, which is lethal. A Jagex Mod Ash success-rate statement on the stall page (60/256 to 300/256, linear) implies certain success from about 82 Agility, so the 85 on the course page is conservative.

Both Jagex Hardcore Worlds posts list only 'The Fremennik Trials (only the 4th phase of the duel with Koschei the Deathless)' as safe; Hardcore Worlds uses the Hardcore Group Ironman death ruleset. The wiki's Koschei and Fremennik Trials pages say forms 1-3 are safe for regular Hardcore Ironmen, which does not apply here.
facts.caveat: Hardcore Worlds launched 2026-11-04 (16 days before verification): new content whose rules Jagex may still revise; re-check the T1 posts before publishing. The wiki pages contain HCIM-safe wording for forms 1-3 (Koschei rev 15387641 line 226; Fremennik Trials rev 15396092 line 218) that planners must not use. Default UNSAFE applies.

facts.subject: Koschei the deathless (The Fremennik Trials)
facts.statement: Koschei's max hits are 3 / 5 / 7 for forms 1-3, each attacking every 4 ticks (2.4 s), with 30 / 50 / 70 Hitpoints. Form 4 hits for at most 1 but every tick (0.6 s), has 255 Hitpoints and 255 Attack: up to 100 damage per minute (computed: 60 s / 0.6 s = 100 hits x 1).
facts.caveat: Second confirmation is partial: the 3/5/7 values appear only on the Koschei page (infobox and its strategy prose, same page); the Fremennik Trials page independently confirms only form 4's 1 damage per tick. No non-wiki source was found. One Koschei-page sentence ('in his third and fourth form he hits progressively harder and quicker') does not match the infobox.

sources.title: Koschei the deathless
sources.quote: His max hits are 3 in his first form, 5 in his second, and 7 in his third.

sources.title: Koschei the deathless
sources.quote: *He is the fastest attacking [[NPC]] in the game (in his final form with an attack speed of 1, meaning every 0.6 seconds), along with [[Scarab swarm]]s. The attack speed for his first three forms is 4 (2.4 seconds), the same as unarmed combat.

sources.title: The Fremennik Trials
sources.quote: The fourth form is the hardest. He will hit once every game tick, but can only hit for 1 damage at a time.

facts.subject: Koschei the deathless, form 4
facts.statement: When Koschei's 4th form starts he drains all your prayer points, then keeps draining them by 1-2 every second, so protection prayers cannot be relied on in form 4.
facts.caveat: Single source for the exact rates (Fremennik Trials walkthrough). The Koschei page change log (6 February 2014: 'Koschei now keeps it drained') supports the drain but gives no numbers.

sources.title: The Fremennik Trials
sources.quote: In this form, Koschei will quickly drop your prayer points in intervals of 1-2 every second and will drop all of your prayer points as soon as the form starts.

sources.quote: |change = After Koschei the Deathless drained your prayer in [[Fremennik Trials]], players could simply restore it and re-activate their prayers. Koschei now keeps it drained.

value.ring_of_life: teleports you to your respawn point and the fight restarts at form 1
value.phase_timer: 10 minutes in one phase, then Koschei despawns and the fight resets

facts.statement: The Koschei fight is in an instance under Thorvald's house. Weapons, armour, fletching materials and runes are not allowed; food, Prayer, god books and jewellery are. A ring of life sends you to your respawn point and you restart at form 1. Spending 10 minutes in one phase makes Koschei disappear and the fight restart. Whether normal teleports or walking out work mid-fight is not documented.

sources.quote: # You cannot use any [[weapons]], [[armour]], [[fletching]] materials (such as [[logs]]/[[arrowtips]]), or bring [[runes]]. ... However, you can use [[food]], [[Prayer]], [[god book]]s, and jewellery.

facts.subject: The Fremennik Trials: Koschei fight arena
facts.value: Koschei can be trapped on the far side of a chasm or by the pillars of fire to regenerate. Staying too long makes him reset to form 1. He can be flinched at the torches.
facts.statement: There is no attack safespot (you have no weapons), but you can trap Koschei on the other side of a hole in the floor or by the fire pillars and regenerate. Staying too long makes him disappear and come back in form 1. He can also be flinched from the north or south tile of a torch.

sources.title: The Fremennik Trials
sources.quote: There is no way to safespot him as you have no weapons, but you can trap him over the hole and wait a while for your health to regenerate. However, if you stay there too long, he will disappear and reappear after you run around, back in his first form.
